title: Interactive regression hub and evidence archive for benchmark triage
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a lightweight interactive ‘Regression Hub’ that combines a compact evidence archive with side-by-side comparison tooling so SREs and perf engineers can quickly validate, reproduce, and document benchmark regressions. The hub will ingest batch benchmark outputs (tokens/sec, p50/p95 latency, memory, KV-cache hit rates) from the benchmark-runner, index them into an evidence store, and surface an interactive diff UI that highlights statistically-significant deltas and provides playback links to exact run artifacts (seeded traffic profile, model variant, kernel config, hardware allocation). The system should support tagging runs, annotating with triage notes, and linking triage outcomes to alerting rules and incident records.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence store accepts JSON benchmark bundles and stores immutable artifacts with unique run IDs
UI displays two runs side-by-side and highlights metrics with >5% change or p95 shifts >10ms by default
Automatic anomaly scorer ranks candidate regressions using signal-to-noise and historical drift (top-5 per day)
Triage flow allows annotating a run, assigning owners, and creating a GitHub issue or an internal incident link
Playback links open a reproducible harness run with the same traffic profile and seed; reproducible run starts within 2 minutes of clicking for archived small runs
Retention: evidence store can be queried by run ID, model, kernel, and commit hash; performance for run lookup is <300ms for indexed fields
technical_notes: Data model: store flat run metadata (all fields as strings) and a manifest list of artifact URIs. Avoid nested JSON in the manifest by normalizing artifacts to a list of URIs with typed prefixes (s3://, gs://, artifacts/redwood://)
Ingestion: use a small ingestion lambda that validates schema, computes deterministic fingerprint (sha256) of key telemetry arrays, and emits to evidence.bucket + Elastic index for fast search
Anomaly scorer: baseline uses Welch's t-test on rolling window of last 30 runs for the same model/config; weight by sample size and recentness; tuned to favor precision over recall for triage inbox
UI: React-based single-page app with a diff engine that computes percentage and absolute deltas and renders sparkline overlays for p50/p95 and tokens/sec distributions
Security: evidence store should be ACL-protected; private deployments must honor VPC-only access and KMS-encrypted artifact storage
Scale: expected ingest rate 200 runs/day initially; design sharding by model-name and date to keep queries sub-300ms
Fallback: if artifact storage is missing, UI surfaces the raw metrics table and a best-effort delta with a banner stating artifacts unavailable
